findings.claim: CG-MAJ-02 from R1 is not closed in the governance canonical: plan §4 020B.1 still lists only three trigger paths (.github/workflows/policy-check.yml, policies/**, tests/workflow/**) and omits schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json. No tracked remediation item (BACKLOG row or future-slice requirement) exists to ensure the plan is ever amended.
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020B.1 row: 'SCP-local job workflow-selftest trigger = pull_request on paths .github/workflows/policy-check.yml, policies/**, tests/workflow/** (blocks merge of any PR touching those paths).' — three paths only. .github/workflows/workflow-selftest.yml lines 5–9: paths: .github/workflows/policy-check.yml, policies/**, tests/workflow/**, schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json — four paths. Fix-round dispatcher-result.json self_reported_concerns: 'docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md was outside the allowed write scope, so the schema-trigger rationale was documented in the in-scope dispatch artifacts rather than in the parent plan row itself.' No BACKLOG.md entry, no future-slice reference in any committed plan document names this gap as requiring resolution.
findings.impact: The plan §4 020B.1 row is the governance canonical for 020B.1 conformance audits. Every subsequent reviewer comparing implementation to plan spec will find an undocumented trigger path. More critically: an implementor following only the plan to recreate or extend the selftest trigger set would omit schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json, creating a CI blind spot where schema changes bypass the selftest gate. The gap is live through all remaining WP-SCP-020 slices since no remediation is scheduled.
findings.mitigation: Amend plan §4 020B.1 trigger-path row to add schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json with rationale '(expected-annotations.json is schema-bound; schema changes must re-validate all fixture expectations)'. This is a one-line documentation edit. It can be combined with the fixture-path input amendment required by R2-CMP-MAJ-02 into a single plan-amendment commit. Open a BACKLOG item or add a pre-dispatch requirement to 020C to confirm this edit lands before 020C review checkpoint.

findings.claim: The fixture-path input added to policy-check.yml during fix-round R1 is not reflected in plan §4 020B AC (i) input enumeration. Plan §4 020B AC (i) is the canonical deliverable specification for the reusable workflow's input surface; it enumerates exactly six inputs. The implementation now has seven. No plan amendment was made and none is scheduled.
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020B AC (i): 'inputs: enumerated with type: — rule-set: string (default: "starter"), threshold: string (default: "deny"), annotate: boolean (default: true), scp_bypass: boolean (default: false), waivers-path: string (default: "output/findings/waivers.json"), rule-config-path: string (default: ".scp/rule-config.yaml").' Six inputs only. .github/workflows/policy-check.yml lines 6–40: seven inputs, including fixture-path: string (default: '.') at lines 37–40. Fix-round dispatch package scope_boundary excluded docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md. Executor self_reported_concerns acknowledge the plan was out of write scope; no tracked remediation item exists. WP-SCP-020 §9 AC 6 ('workflow-selftest green on pass + fail fixtures') implicitly depends on fixture-path being present, but the AC text makes no mention of it.
findings.impact: A post-WP completeness audit comparing implementation to plan §4 020B AC (i) will flag fixture-path as undocumented scope. More critically, downstream adopters reading the plan for the canonical input surface will not see fixture-path and may not know it exists. Adopters who want to scope policy evaluation to a subdirectory (a valid use case given the input's default-'.'-semantics) have no plan-level pointer to this capability.
findings.mitigation: Amend plan §4 020B AC (i) to add 'fixture-path: string (default: ".") — restricts changed-file discovery to a path prefix; defaults to whole-repo evaluation for normal callers; used by the selftest harness to achieve fixture-tree isolation.' This amendment can be batched with the R2-CMP-MAJ-01 trigger-path fix into a single plan edit commit before 020C opens.

findings.claim: Oracle tautology (020B1-SBP-001) is closed for same-PR co-edits but a staged two-PR attack remains viable post-020C. The compensating control — CODEOWNERS on tests/workflow/** — is deferred to 020K but is not enumerated in plan §4 020K's CODEOWNERS path list, so there is no governance guarantee it will land there.
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 67–81: ratchet check guards only the case where services_path in changed AND expected_path in changed AND exists_at(base, services_path) AND exists_at(base, expected_path). A staged attack: PR-A changes only fixture-fail/services.yml to a compliant shape (passes ratchet, changes only one of the pair); PR-B subsequently changes only fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json to empty findings (passes ratchet, only one of the pair). After both PRs merge, fixture-fail expects empty findings and services.yml is compliant — selftest passes, oracle is neutralized. docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020K CODEOWNERS path list: 'policies/**, renovate/**, .github/workflows/**, docs/DECISIONS.md, output/findings/waivers.json' — tests/workflow/** is absent. The R1 review noted tests/workflow/** must be added to 020K scope; this has not been acted on.
findings.impact: From 020C merge (when fixture-fail/expected-annotations.json contains real deny findings) until 020K merge (when CODEOWNERS is wired), anyone with write access to the repository can execute the two-PR staged attack without a designated-reviewer gate. The window spans at least slices 020C through 020J — several months of exposure. After 020K, the attack still requires CODEOWNERS approval of both PRs, which is a strong compensating control, but only if tests/workflow/** is in the 020K CODEOWNERS list.
findings.mitigation: Add tests/workflow/** to plan §4 020K CODEOWNERS path list explicitly: 'tests/workflow/** — oracle files for the selftest harness; mutations require named-reviewer sign-off.' Add a note to conftest.md: 'Note: tests/workflow/** will be covered by CODEOWNERS in slice 020K. Until that slice merges, oracle file changes require manual review discipline.' This ensures the 020K implementor does not overlook the path.

findings.claim: fixture-fail/services.yml contains the field waiver_ref: W-020B1-SELFTEST which is not a field defined in the SVC-003 mode-set accepted_modes schema, is not documented in conftest.md, and has no corresponding waivers document anywhere in the repository. If SCP-R-001 (020C) validates accepted_modes entries strictly (no additional properties), this field will cause an unexpected deny finding on a different rule violation path than the one the fixture is designed to test.
findings.evidence: tests/workflow/fixture-fail/services.yml lines 14–17: accepted_modes entry is {mode: mode.bearer_legacy, deprecation_close_date: '2099-12-31', waiver_ref: W-020B1-SELFTEST}. docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020C: SCP-R-001 validates 'services.yml root-shape conformance to pre-D-021 SVC-003 mode set (mode.user_oidc, mode.service_rs256, mode.api_key, mode.bearer_legacy); deprecation_close_date ∈ {"2026-06-30", "2026-09-30"}.' The plan does not enumerate waiver_ref as a valid field. No waivers.json or DECISIONS.md entry references W-020B1-SELFTEST. conftest.md does not mention waiver_ref or explain its purpose. Fix-round dispatcher-result.json: 'Pre-positioned the fail fixture with a future-rule violation shape' — no mention of waiver_ref.
findings.impact: If SCP-R-001 validates accepted_modes entries with additionalProperties: false (a common strict-schema pattern), the waiver_ref field will trigger a deny finding with a message about unexpected field rather than about mode.bearer_legacy deprecation_close_date. This makes fixture-fail's deny summary ambiguous — it fails for the wrong reason — and the 020C transition would require fixing the fixture-fail shape rather than just flipping expected-annotations.json. The pre-positioned forward-reference to W-020B1-SELFTEST also creates a false impression that a waiver for this fixture already exists.
findings.mitigation: Either (a) remove waiver_ref from fixture-fail/services.yml and add a YAML comment: '# mode.bearer_legacy with out-of-range deprecation_close_date: SCP-R-001 will deny this once 020C ships'; or (b) confirm in conftest.md and the 020C dispatch package that SCP-R-001 will not validate waiver_ref (because it is at the mode-entry level and the rule only checks mode and deprecation_close_date fields). If (b), add a note to conftest.md explaining waiver_ref is a non-enforced annotation. Resolve before 020C dispatch opens.

findings.claim: The fixture-path input description in policy-check.yml implies the input is only for selftest harness use, which misrepresents it as a general-purpose scoping mechanism available to any caller.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml lines 37–40: description: 'Restrict changed-file discovery to a fixture subtree when the selftest harness invokes the workflow.' The phrase 'when the selftest harness invokes the workflow' scopes this as a harness-only feature. Default is '.' and the validation logic is general-purpose: any caller could pass a subdirectory to scope evaluation. ADOPT-001 §12 (planned in 020H part 3) will document the input surface; if this description ships as-is, adopters who read it will not recognise the subdirectory-scoping capability.
findings.impact: Low. No runtime regression. An adopter wanting to scope evaluation to a monorepo subdirectory would not discover this input from its description. The capability exists but is undiscoverable.
findings.mitigation: Rephrase the description: 'Restrict changed-file discovery to a path prefix. Defaults to "." (whole-repository evaluation). Set to a fixture directory path when invoking from a test harness, or to a subdirectory when the caller wants to scope evaluation to a monorepo package.'

findings.claim: The oracle ratchet's asymmetric treatment of new versus existing fixture pairs is undocumented in conftest.md. New fixture pairs may freely set both services.yml and expected-annotations.json in one PR; existing pairs may not. A contributor adding a new fixture pair will not know this asymmetry or its governance implication (new pairs start with weaker oracle protection).
findings.evidence: workflow-selftest.yml lines 73–80: ratchet condition includes exists_at(base, services_path) AND exists_at(base, expected_path). A new fixture pair has neither file at base, so exists_at returns False for both; the ratchet is bypassed. conftest.md documents the ratchet behavior ('Existing fixture pairs are ratcheted: a PR may not change both services.yml and expected-annotations.json for the same committed fixture in one change') but does not call out the new-pair exception.
findings.impact: Very low. Design-correct behavior for bootstrapping new fixtures. However, a future contributor introducing a low-quality new fixture pair with a trivially-passing expected oracle would not be warned that their pair starts unratcheted until the next review cycle flags it.
findings.mitigation: Add one sentence to conftest.md after the ratchet description: 'New fixture pairs introduced for the first time may include both files in one PR; the ratchet applies only to pairs that already exist at the PR base.'
